note: 23 motors now take a different published file, 14 of them with a different curve or mass: the check that a file agrees with the motor's certified impulse now measures the curve the app flies, and a tie between two files no longer depends on the order thrustcurve.org lists them (in v0.143 that order alone changed a Hypertek motor's loaded mass by 10 percent). Re-open a design flying one of them from its file, or re-pick the motor in every flight configuration that flies it; reloading the page keeps the old curve. The impulse warning now describes the curve flown (the E16W's warning was false; the J570W, 6 percent over, now has one). Most RockSim bulkheads with a hole now weigh what RockSim weighs (one baffle still flies solid), and .rkt saves carry a stage's known mass. Four more AeroTech motors (H219T, J1265T, L1365M, I40N-P) fill their nozzle exit from AeroTech's own papers. A page that cannot start now says so with a Reload button instead of staying blank, and an offline failure says it could not reach thrustcurve.org instead of claiming a motor has no curve. GZIP .ork files open, and a .ork motor with no delay flies plugged, as desktop reads it. Batch simulate gives a time estimate and refuses a sweep over 20,000 flights. Fins on a boat tail are drawn on the surface; a nose cone, body tube or transition saved without a length, or a tube or nose cone without a radius, is drawn at the size the simulator flies.
